## Repair Request for Toronto Rental

Here’s a polite, firm email you can send to your landlord. It states the facts clearly, requests a repair timeline, and keeps the tone cooperative.

## Email Draft

**Subject:** Request for Repairs: Bathroom Ceiling Leak and Heating Issues

Dear [Landlord’s Name],

I hope you are well. I am writing to let you know about two maintenance issues in the unit that need attention.

First, there is a leak in the bathroom ceiling that appeared on **2026-01-14** after heavy rain. Second, the heating has been intermittent and has occurred **4 times in the last 2 months**. Since my lease began on **2025-11-01**, I have paid rent on time and wanted to bring these issues to your attention promptly so they can be resolved as soon as possible.

I would appreciate it if these repairs could be scheduled **within the next 7 days**. I am happy to coordinate access at a convenient time. Please let me know the next steps and when someone can attend to inspect and repair both issues.

I want to document this respectfully and keep things straightforward, as my goal is simply to have the unit maintained properly and avoid any further damage or discomfort.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your response.

Kind regards,
[Your Full Name]
[Unit Number]
[Phone Number]

## Attachments to Include

- Photos of the bathroom ceiling leak, including close-up and wide shots
- A photo showing the date if visible, or a note with the date taken
- Photos of any water stains, peeling paint, bubbling drywall, or discoloration
- A short log of each heating issue, including date, time, and how long it lasted
- Notes on indoor temperature during heating outages, if available
- Any prior messages to the landlord about these issues
- A brief timeline of the leak starting on **2026-01-14** after heavy rain

## Quick Actions
